title: Space Tech Briefing — September 24, 2026
summary:
Good morning, space enthusiasts and future explorers! This is your daily dose of the cosmos, live from the Space Technology broadcast desk, and it is Thursday, September 24, 2026. Get ready to launch into a thrilling morning as we bring you the latest and greatest from beyond our atmosphere and right here on Earth!

First up, an incredible scientific discovery that has rocked the lunar landscape! Scientists, utilizing sharp imagery from NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter – that's LRO for short – have just announced the identification of the largest impact crater found on the Moon in a century! This isn't just any dent; we're talking about a massive new crater, 222 meters in diameter, surrounded by a distinct seven-kilometer-wide "cold spot." It plunges approximately 43 meters deep into the lunar surface. Researchers pinpoint its formation to a relatively recent event, occurring between April 11 and May 22, 2024, when an asteroid or comet, roughly the size of a three to six-story building, slammed into our celestial neighbor. This significant landmark has been officially named in tribute to the American scientist Tom McGetchin, a pioneering geologist and planetologist renowned for his work on impact craters. A monumental discovery, truly showing us the Moon is still full of surprises!

And now, from real-world impacts to cinematic masterpieces! If you love space and film, then you'll be thrilled to hear about an exceptional retrospective happening right now. The Cinémathèque de Paris Bercy is inviting us on a journey through 120 years of spatial cinema! This incredible program, titled "Cinema and Space: The Essentials," spans from the mind-bending "2001: A Space Odyssey" to the heartwarming "Wall-E," and even the terrifying depths of "Alien." It's a comprehensive look at how the cosmos has inspired storytellers for over a century, and the best part? The screenings and discussions are animated by experts from the French space agency, CNES! A fantastic way to connect our fascination with space to the art of storytelling.

What a morning, packed with both groundbreaking science and stellar cultural events! Thank you for joining us on this cosmic ride. Stay curious, keep looking up, and we'll be back tomorrow with more exciting updates from the universe. Until then, have a magnificent day!
